beats.title: Cai Lun Presents Paper to the Court
beats.description: A Chinese court official reported a new writing material made from bark, rags and fishing nets, cheaper than silk or bamboo.
beats.why_in: writing surface that made printing possible
beats.note: Traditional date of presentation to the emperor

beats.title: Trajan's Column Is Inscribed
beats.description: Roman stonecutters carved a monument base with letters so well proportioned that designers still copy them as a model of capitals.

beats.title: Diamond Sutra Printed in China
beats.description: A scroll of Buddhist scripture was printed from carved woodblocks and is the oldest dated printed book known.

beats.title: Bi Sheng Invents Movable Type
beats.description: A Chinese commoner shaped individual characters from baked clay so they could be rearranged and reused to print pages.

beats.title: Jikji Printed with Metal Type
beats.description: Buddhist teachings were printed in a Korean temple using cast metal characters, decades before any Western press.

beats.title: Gutenberg Bible Printed
beats.description: A German goldsmith's press produced a large run of handsome Bibles using movable metal type, launching printing in Europe.

beats.title: First Roman Type Printed in Italy
beats.description: Two German printers set up a press in a monastery near Rome and brought printing south of the Alps.

beats.title: Jenson Cuts His Roman Typeface
beats.description: A Venetian printer produced an elegant roman letter whose proportions still inspire revivals today.
beats.note: First book in his roman type 1470

beats.title: Caxton Opens England's First Press
beats.description: A merchant who had learned printing abroad opened a press in Westminster and began issuing books in English.

beats.title: Aldus Introduces Italic Type
beats.description: A Venetian printer introduced a slanted, compact letter to fit small pocket-sized editions of classical authors.

beats.title: Garamond's Roman Type Appears
beats.description: A Parisian punchcutter's refined roman letters were used in a scholarly edition and became a model for centuries.

beats.title: First Press in the Americas
beats.description: A printer set up a press in a colonial capital and produced religious texts for the New World.

beats.title: First Printed Newspaper Appears
beats.description: A Strasbourg printer began publishing a regular weekly sheet of news, the first of its kind.

beats.title: Bay Psalm Book Printed
beats.description: A press in a New England colony produced a hymn book, the first book printed in English-speaking North America.

beats.title: Henry Mill's Typewriter Patent
beats.description: An English engineer won a patent for a machine to impress letters singly on paper, the earliest recorded typewriter idea.

beats.title: Caslon Issues His Type Specimen
beats.description: An English engraver showed off his oldstyle typefaces, which quickly dominated printing across Britain and its colonies.

beats.title: Baskerville Prints Virgil
beats.description: A Birmingham printer published a book showing off his sharp, high-contrast typeface and glossy paper.

beats.title: Senefelder Invents Lithography
beats.description: A Bavarian playwright found that grease and water could be used to print from a flat stone.

beats.title: Steam Press Prints The Times
beats.description: A London newspaper was run off on a steam-driven cylinder press, multiplying output many times over.

beats.title: First Sans-Serif Typeface Shown
beats.description: A London type foundry issued a bold, plain letter with no serifs, which shocked contemporaries.

beats.title: Louis Braille Devises His Alphabet
beats.description: A blind French teenager developed a code of raised dots that could be read by touch.

beats.title: Hoe Patents the Rotary Press
beats.description: An American inventor mounted type on a revolving cylinder, allowing newspapers to print at far greater speed.

beats.title: Sholes Typewriter Patented
beats.description: A Milwaukee newspaper man won a patent for a practical keyboard writing machine.

beats.title: Remington Sells Typewriters
beats.description: A gun maker put the first commercial typewriter on the market, with the QWERTY layout.

beats.title: Linotype Machine Debuts
beats.description: A newspaper in New York began setting whole lines of metal type from a keyboard, speeding up typesetting.

beats.title: Offset Printing Adopted
beats.description: A New Jersey printer found that printing from a rubber blanket gave sharper results, creating a technique that now dominates.

beats.title: Johnston Typeface for London
beats.description: A calligrapher drew a clear, humanist sans-serif alphabet for a city's railway signs and posters.

beats.title: Futura Released
beats.description: A German designer issued a geometric typeface built from circles, triangles and squares, which became a modernist favourite.

beats.title: Gill Sans Released
beats.description: An English sculptor and letterer's clean sans-serif typeface was issued and became a British staple.

beats.title: Times New Roman Debuts
beats.description: A London newspaper commissioned a tightly spaced new typeface that would later become a word-processing default.

beats.title: Helvetica Released
beats.description: A Swiss foundry issued a neutral sans-serif typeface that spread across corporate logos and street signs worldwide.

beats.title: IBM Selectric Typewriter Launched
beats.description: An electric typewriter replaced moving typebars with a spinning ball, letting users swap fonts in seconds.

beats.title: Project Gutenberg Begins
beats.description: A student typed out a famous declaration to share on a university computer, starting the free electronic book library.

beats.title: Adobe Systems Founded
beats.description: Two Xerox researchers started a software company that would transform how type is drawn and printed.

beats.title: Desktop Publishing Arrives
beats.description: A laser printer, PostScript and page layout software let ordinary offices produce typeset-quality pages from a desk.

beats.title: Unicode Standard First Published
beats.description: A consortium released a universal character encoding aiming to give every writing system's letters a unique number.

beats.title: Comic Sans Created
beats.description: A Microsoft designer drew a casual, comic-book style typeface that became both popular and widely mocked.

beats.title: Verdana Released for the Screen
beats.description: A typeface with wide letters and generous spacing was drawn specifically to stay legible at small sizes on computer displays.

beats.title: Calibri Becomes the Default Font
beats.description: A softly rounded typeface replaced the long-time standard in a major office software suite.

beats.title: Emoji Added to Unicode
beats.description: The universal text standard adopted hundreds of Japanese-origin pictograms, making them part of everyday writing worldwide.
